en.html:
The next morning.

More than twenty young men of the village had been mobilized, and the refilling of the tunnel—or the performance of it—was going smoothly. A few narrow side passages had actually been crushed.

The magistrate's party must have noticed by now. They could not fail to.

Some reaction was bound to come soon...

　代官らは既に気付いているだろう。
　気付かないわけがない。

　もうじき、何らかの反応を見せる筈だ……。

I exchanged farewells with Kanae and her attendant, who were ready to leave.

From here they were to go back to the occupation forces' headquarters, taking as much time as possible and wandering by detours. That was the inspector's last support to us.

At my answer, Kanae Ootori gave a small laugh.

en.html:
Sayo"Miss, Mr. Minato, kindly stop making these farewells so damp. This Sayo thinks you will be meeting again before very long."
Kanae"Oh, Nanny thinks so too? Actually, so do I. Somehow I do not feel that my bond with Kageaki ends here."
Kageaki"I am honored that you think so."
Kanae"That is why, Kageaki—let us meet again."
Kageaki"...Yes. If fate allows, again."
Sayo"Mr. Minato. Good fortune in battle."
Kageaki"Thank you. May Sayo ji also keep well."

en.html:
弥源太"Well. The rest depends on heaven's luck. Which comes first, the new inspector or the end of the magistrate's patience..."
Kageaki"Indeed. Magistrate Nagasaka's short temper is the key to the contest."
弥源太"Then our chances are not bad. Patience that fellow has, certainly—as much as a rabbit has tail."
Kageaki"If Lieutenant Ootori's superior, in turn, had a snake's body worth of patience and waited quietly for her return, success would be almost assured."
弥源太"That much we cannot hope for. Whatever happens, something will surely stir before the day is out."
Kageaki"Yes."
ふき"Grandpaaaa! Warrior sahiiib!"

景明 「如何にも。 　長坂代官の気の短さが勝負の鍵となります」
弥源太 「ならば分は悪くないな。 　あやつめの気はせいぜいが兎の尻尾ほどの 長さよ」
景明 「加えて大鳥中尉の上官の気が蛇の体長ほど もあり、中尉の帰還を辛抱強く待ってくれて いれば、成功はまず確約されていると言える のですが」
弥源太 「そこまでは期待できんかな。 　しかし何にしろ、今日中には必ず何らかの 動きがあろうよ」
景明 「は」
ふき 「じっちゃまー。 　お武家さまー」

ふき"Warrior sahib... was it a nuisance?"
Kageaki"Thank you. I was just feeling hungry."
弥源太"...True. A man cannot fight on an empty stomach. Let us accept."
ふな"Eat!"
ふき"Funa! You do not tell guests 'Eat!' like that! ...Well then, please. It is only rice balls. Oh, and this is tea."
Kageaki"Everything has been thought of. Fuki, you have taken very good care of us."
ふき"...E-eh..."
弥源太"Do not praise her too much, Mido. After this, how shall the rest of us get a word in?"
ふき"G-Grandpa!"
弥源太"Heh-heh..."
